papers.title: Effect of thermal ablation on persistent HPV infection in Danish women ≥ 40 years of age: a quasi-randomized clinical study
papers.abstract: Thermal ablation is a cervical heat treatment that destroys a defined area of the cervix. We evaluated whether thermal ablation facilitates HPV clearance in women with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection, using HPV status and FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA methylation as molecular markers for treatment efficacy. A total of 131 women aged ≥ 40 years with persistent HR-HPV infection but without histologically confirmed high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (≥ CIN2) were enrolled at three outpatient gynecological clinics. After exclusions, 39 women were allocated to the intervention arm (thermal ablation) and 34 to the no treatment only control arm. Allocation was based on date of birth (even dates: intervention; odd dates: control), using quasi-randomization. HPV genotyping and FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status were assessed at baseline (0 months), 3 months, and 10 months. Thermal ablation was performed using the WISAP probe at 65 °C for 2 min and at 100 °C for 40 s, administered across two sessions 2–3 days apart. At 10 months, 64.1% of women in the intervention arm and 79.4% in the control arm remained HR-HPV positive. No significant difference in HPV positivity was observed between arms at any time point. FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation positivity showed a transient decrease in the intervention arm (-10.2%) at 3 months but increased in both arms over 10 months to above baseline levels, with no significant treatment effect. Thermal ablation does not facilitate HPV clearance in women with persistent HR-HPV infection without significant cervical disease. Methylation positivity increased over time in both study arms, consistent with ongoing oncogenic transformation. Women treated with thermal ablation remain HR-HPV positive and require continued surveillance, indicating no clinical benefit over observation alone. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07376031, registered 21 January 2026. Thermal ablation does not significantly affect HPV clearance or FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status in women ≥40 years with persistent high-risk HPV infection without significant cervical disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in women aged ≥40 years poses a risk for progression to cervical disease despite the absence of high-grade lesions. The study aimed to determine whether thermal ablation facilitates HPV clearance in this population using HPV status and FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA methylation as molecular markers for treatment efficacy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A quasi-randomized clinical study enrolled 131 women aged ≥40 years with persistent HR-HPV infection but without histologically confirmed high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (≥CIN2) across three outpatient gynecological clinics. After exclusions, 39 women were allocated to thermal ablation and 34 to a no-treatment control arm using quasi-randomization based on date of birth.
analysis.methods: HPV genotyping and FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 10 months. Thermal ablation was performed using the WISAP probe at 65 °C for 2 minutes and at 100 °C for 40 seconds, administered across two sessions 2–3 days apart.
analysis.main_results: At 10 months, 64.1% of women in the intervention arm and 79.4% in the control arm remained HR-HPV positive, with no significant difference between arms at any time point. FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation positivity showed a transient decrease (-10.2%) in the intervention arm at 3 months but increased in both arms over 10 months to above baseline levels, with no significant treatment effect.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that thermal ablation does not facilitate HPV clearance or reduce oncogenic transformation risk in women with persistent HR-HPV infection without significant cervical disease, as evidenced by sustained HPV positivity and increasing methylation positivity in both arms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that thermal ablation does not provide clinical benefit over observation alone for HPV clearance in this population, indicating that continued surveillance remains necessary and that alternative strategies should be explored for persistent HR-HPV infection in women ≥40 years.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s quasi-randomized design and lack of histological confirmation of high-grade lesions limit causal inference and generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to small sample size, absence of blinding, and reliance on molecular markers rather than clinical endpoints.

analysis.summary_en: This quasi-randomized clinical study evaluated whether thermal ablation facilitates HPV clearance in 73 women aged ≥40 years with persistent high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) infection but without high-grade cervical lesions. Participants were allocated to thermal ablation (n=39) or no treatment (n=34) and followed for 10 months. HPV genotyping and FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 10 months. Thermal ablation was performed using a WISAP probe at 65 °C for 2 minutes and 100 °C for 40 seconds across two sessions. At 10 months, 64.1% in the intervention arm and 79.4% in the control arm remained HR-HPV positive, with no significant difference between arms. Methylation positivity transiently decreased in the intervention arm at 3 months but increased in both arms to above baseline levels by 10 months, indicating no treatment effect. The authors concluded that thermal ablation does not facilitate HPV clearance or reduce oncogenic transformation risk in this population, underscoring the need for continued surveillance and alternative management strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管没有高级别病变,但年龄≥40岁的女性持续高危人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV)感染仍存在进展为宫颈疾病的风险。该研究旨在利用 HPV 状态和 FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA 甲基化作为 治疗 功效的分子标记,确定热消融是否有助于该人群的 HPV 清除。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项半随机临床研究在三个妇科门诊招募了 131 名年龄≥40 岁、持续 HR-HPV 感染但无组织学证实的高级别宫颈上皮内瘤变 (≥CIN2) 的女性。排除后,39 名女性被分配到热消融组,34 名女性被分配到非 治疗 对照组,使用基于出生日期的准随机化。
elements_zh.methods: 在基线、3 个月和 10 个月时评估 HPV 基因分型和 FAM19A4/miR124-2 甲基化状态。使用 WISAP 探头在 65 °C 下进行热消融 2 分钟,在 100 °C 下进行 40 秒,分两次进行,间隔 2-3 天。
elements_zh.main_results: 10 个月时,干预组中 64.1% 的女性和对照组中 79.4% 的女性仍保持 HR-HPV 阳性,两组之间在任何时间点都没有显着差异。FAM19A4/miR124-2 甲基化阳性率在 3 个月时在干预组中显示短暂下降 (-10.2%),但在 10 个月后两组中均增加至基线水平以上,但没有显着的 治疗 效应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,对于持续性 HR-HPV 感染但无明显宫颈疾病的女性,热消融不会促进 HPV 清除或降低致癌转化风险,正如双臂持续 HPV 阳性和甲基化阳性增加所证明的那样。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,对于该人群中的 HPV 清除,热消融并没有比单独观察提供临床益处,这表明持续的 监测 仍然是必要的,并且应探索针对 ≥ 40 岁女性持续性 HR-HPV 感染的替代策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的准随机设计和缺乏对高级病变的组织学确认限制了因果推断和普遍性。由于样本量小、未实施盲法以及依赖分子标志物而不是临床终点,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 热消融对 40 岁以上丹麦女性持续性 HPV 感染的影响:一项半随机临床研究
papers.source_body_en: Thermal ablation is a cervical heat treatment that destroys a defined area of the cervix. We evaluated whether thermal ablation facilitates HPV clearance in women with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection, using HPV status and FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA methylation as molecular markers for treatment efficacy. A total of 131 women aged ≥ 40 years with persistent HR-HPV infection but without histologically confirmed high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (≥ CIN2) were enrolled at three outpatient gynecological clinics. After exclusions, 39 women were allocated to the intervention arm (thermal ablation) and 34 to the no treatment only control arm. Allocation was based on date of birth (even dates: intervention; odd dates: control), using quasi-randomization. HPV genotyping and FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status were assessed at baseline (0 months), 3 months, and 10 months. Thermal ablation was performed using the WISAP probe at 65 °C for 2 min and at 100 °C for 40 s, administered across two sessions 2–3 days apart. At 10 months, 64.1% of women in the intervention arm and 79.4% in the control arm remained HR-HPV positive. No significant difference in HPV positivity was observed between arms at any time point. FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation positivity showed a transient decrease in the intervention arm (-10.2%) at 3 months but increased in both arms over 10 months to above baseline levels, with no significant treatment effect. Thermal ablation does not facilitate HPV clearance in women with persistent HR-HPV infection without significant cervical disease. Methylation positivity increased over time in both study arms, consistent with ongoing oncogenic transformation. Women treated with thermal ablation remain HR-HPV positive and require continued surveillance, indicating no clinical benefit over observation alone. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07376031, registered 21 January 2026. Thermal ablation does not significantly affect HPV clearance or FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status in women ≥40 years with persistent high-risk HPV infection without significant cervical disease.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管没有高级别病变,但年龄≥40岁的女性持续高危人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV)感染仍存在进展为宫颈疾病的风险。该研究旨在利用 HPV 状态和 FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA 甲基化作为 治疗 功效的分子标记,确定热消融是否有助于该人群的 HPV 清除。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项半随机临床研究在三个妇科门诊招募了 131 名年龄≥40 岁、持续 HR-HPV 感染但无组织学证实的高级别宫颈上皮内瘤变 (≥CIN2) 的女性。排除后,39 名女性被分配到热消融组,34 名女性被分配到非 治疗 对照组,使用基于出生日期的准随机化。
analysis_zh.methods: 在基线、3 个月和 10 个月时评估 HPV 基因分型和 FAM19A4/miR124-2 甲基化状态。使用 WISAP 探头在 65 °C 下进行热消融 2 分钟,在 100 °C 下进行 40 秒,分两次进行,间隔 2-3 天。
analysis_zh.main_results: 10 个月时,干预组中 64.1% 的女性和对照组中 79.4% 的女性仍保持 HR-HPV 阳性,两组之间在任何时间点都没有显着差异。FAM19A4/miR124-2 甲基化阳性率在 3 个月时在干预组中显示短暂下降 (-10.2%),但在 10 个月后两组中均增加至基线水平以上,但没有显着的 治疗 效应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,对于持续性 HR-HPV 感染但无明显宫颈疾病的女性,热消融不会促进 HPV 清除或降低致癌转化风险,正如双臂持续 HPV 阳性和甲基化阳性增加所证明的那样。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,对于该人群中的 HPV 清除,热消融并没有比单独观察提供临床益处,这表明持续的 监测 仍然是必要的,并且应探索针对 ≥ 40 岁女性持续性 HR-HPV 感染的替代策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的准随机设计和缺乏对高级病变的组织学确认限制了因果推断和普遍性。由于样本量小、未实施盲法以及依赖分子标志物而不是临床终点,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Effects of School-Entry Vaccination Mandates on Adolescent Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Uptake: United States, 2008-2023.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between school-entry vaccination mandates and adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination uptake in the United States. We conducted a quasi-experimental study using a difference-in-differences approach comparing HPV vaccination uptake (≥ 1 dose) in mandate (n = 4) versus nonmandate (n = 47) states and territories by sex. We used provider-verified vaccination records from the 2008-2023 National Immunization Survey-Teen (n = 240 616) for adolescents aged 13 to 17 years. Models accounted for staggered policy implementation and adjusted for demographic and socioeconomic covariates. School-entry mandates were associated with 6.4 percentage-points (95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.6, 9.1) higher HPV vaccination uptake among girls and 3.4 percentage points (95% CI = 1.8, 5.0) higher uptake among boys. Associations with HPV vaccination uptake increased over time for girls, whereas for boys, associations were concentrated in the first few years following implementation and attenuated thereafter. School-entry mandates are associated with higher HPV vaccination uptake among adolescents. Public Health Implications. Although mandates alone are unlikely to achieve national HPV vaccination targets, they may serve as an important component of comprehensive state efforts to increase uptake and prevent HPV-related cancers. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print August 20, 2026:e1-e4. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308635).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed why HPV vaccination uptake among adolescents in the United States remained suboptimal despite national recommendations, identifying a gap in understanding the impact of state-level school-entry vaccination mandates on improving coverage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A quasi-experimental difference-in-differences study compared HPV vaccination uptake (≥1 dose) between four mandate states and 47 nonmandate states and territories using provider-verified records from the 2008–2023 National Immunization Survey-Teen for adolescents aged 13 to 17 years.
analysis.methods: The analysis accounted for staggered policy implementation and adjusted for demographic and socioeconomic covariates using provider-verified vaccination records from the National Immunization Survey-Teen.
analysis.main_results: School-entry mandates were associated with 6.4 percentage points (95% CI = 3.6, 9.1) higher HPV vaccination uptake among girls and 3.4 percentage points (95% CI = 1.8, 5.0) higher uptake among boys.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that mandates are associated with higher HPV vaccination uptake, noting that associations strengthened over time for girls but attenuated for boys after initial implementation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests school-entry mandates may serve as an important component of state-level strategies to increase HPV vaccination uptake and reduce HPV-related cancers, though mandates alone are unlikely to achieve national targets.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is moderate in strength due to the quasi-experimental design, potential unmeasured confounding, and reliance on provider-verified records, limiting causal inference and generalizability beyond the included states and territories.

analysis.summary_en: This quasi-experimental study evaluated the association between school-entry HPV vaccination mandates and adolescent vaccination uptake in the United States from 2008 to 2023 using provider-verified records from the National Immunization Survey-Teen. Mandates were associated with a 6.4 percentage-point increase in uptake among girls and a 3.4 percentage-point increase among boys. Associations strengthened over time for girls but attenuated for boys after initial implementation. The authors conclude that mandates may be a valuable component of broader efforts to increase HPV vaccination coverage and reduce HPV-related cancers, though they are unlikely to achieve national targets alone. The study’s moderate evidence strength reflects its quasi-experimental design, potential confounding, and reliance on verified records.

papers.title: HPV16 Genomic Status Stratifies Risk of Disease Recurrence in Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose: A subset of patients with human papillomavirus (HPV)–positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) develops disease recurrence despite generally favorable outcomes. Reliable biomarkers for risk stratification remain lacking. We investigated whether comprehensive viral genomic profiling refines prognostic classification. Experimental Design: Tumor samples from 100 patients with p16-positive and HPV DNA–positive OPSCC enrolled in 2 independent cohorts were analyzed using targeted viral capture sequencing. Viral genotype, sublineage, single-nucleotide variation, virus–host integration sites, viral structural variants (SV), clonality, and viral copy number were characterized. Associations with cumulative incidence of progression, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival were assessed at 60 months. Results: HPV16 was detected in 94 tumors, 83 of which belonged to the HPV16_A1 sublineage. Within this sublineage, 20 tumors harbored strictly episomal viral genomes, whereas 63 exhibited integration and/or viral SV. No progression events occurred in the strictly episomal HPV16_A1 subgroup, whereas 12 occurred among HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. At 60 months, no progression events were observed in strictly episomal HPV16_A1 tumors compared with a 23.1% cumulative incidence of progression in HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. Previously reported high-risk single-nucleotide variants and a novel upstream regulatory region variant were associated with worse PFS. Integration sites were enriched in open chromatin and promoter regions and clustered within viral E2 and E4 genes. Conclusions: Within HPV16_A1 tumors, viral genomic architecture defines clinically distinct subgroups. Strictly episomal (wild-type) genomes identify a low-risk population, whereas integration and SV characterize higher-risk disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: A subset of patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) experiences disease recurrence despite generally favorable outcomes, and reliable biomarkers for risk stratification remain lacking.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Tumor samples from 100 patients with p16-positive and HPV DNA–positive OPSCC enrolled in 2 independent cohorts were analyzed using targeted viral capture sequencing.
analysis.methods: Viral genotype, sublineage, single-nucleotide variation, virus–host integration sites, viral structural variants, clonality, and viral copy number were characterized, and associations with cumulative incidence of progression, progression-free survival, and overall survival were assessed at 60 months.
analysis.main_results: HPV16 was detected in 94 tumors, with 83 belonging to the HPV16_A1 sublineage; within this sublineage, 20 tumors had strictly episomal genomes and 63 exhibited integration and/or viral structural variants, and no progression events occurred in the strictly episomal subgroup compared with a 23.1% cumulative incidence in the integration/SV subgroup at 60 months.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Within HPV16_A1 tumors, viral genomic architecture defines clinically distinct subgroups, with strictly episomal genomes identifying a low-risk population and integration/SV characterizing higher-risk disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that viral genomic profiling could refine prognostic classification in HPV16_A1–positive OPSCC, potentially guiding surveillance intensity and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, single-virus focus on HPV16_A1, and reliance on targeted sequencing, warranting prospective validation and broader genomic analyses to confirm generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether viral genomic profiling can refine risk stratification in HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). Tumor samples from 100 p16-positive and HPV DNA–positive OPSCC patients across two cohorts underwent targeted viral capture sequencing to characterize HPV16 genotype, sublineage, mutations, integration sites, structural variants, clonality, and viral copy number. Within the HPV16_A1 sublineage, tumors with strictly episomal genomes showed no progression events over 60 months, whereas those with viral integration or structural variants had a 23.1% cumulative incidence of progression. The authors conclude that viral genomic architecture stratifies risk, identifying episomal genomes as low-risk and integration/SV as higher-risk. These findings suggest potential utility for viral genomic profiling in guiding surveillance and treatment decisions, though limitations include retrospective design, single-virus focus, and targeted sequencing, necessitating prospective validation.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的:尽管预后总体良好,但 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 阳性口咽鳞状细胞癌 (OPSCC) 患者的一部分仍会出现疾病复发。仍然缺乏用于风险分层的可靠生物标志物。我们研究了全面的病毒基因组分析是否可以改善预后分类。实验设计:使用靶向病毒捕获测序对参加 2 个独立 队列研究 的 100 名 p16 阳性和 HPV DNA 阳性 OPSCC 患者的肿瘤样本进行分析。对病毒基因型、亚系、单核苷酸变异、病毒-宿主整合位点、病毒结构变异(SV)、克隆性和病毒拷贝数进行了表征。在 60 个月时评估与累积 发病率 进展、无进展生存期 (PFS) 和总生存期的关联。结果:94个肿瘤中检测到HPV16,其中83个属于HPV16_A1亚系。在该亚系中,20 个肿瘤具有严格附加型病毒 基因组,而 63 个则表现出整合和/或病毒 SV。在严格附加型 HPV16_A1 亚组中没有发生进展事件,而在具有整合和/或 SV 的 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中发生了 12 起进展事件。60 个月时,在严格附加型 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中没有观察到进展事件,而在具有整合和/或 SV 的 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中,累积进展 发病率 为 23.1%。先前报道的高风险单核苷酸变异和新型上游调控区变异与较差的 PFS 相关。整合位点在开放染色质和启动子区域富集,并聚集在病毒 E2 和 E4 基因内。结论:在 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中,病毒基因组结构定义了临床上不同的亚组。严格附加型(野生型)基因组 识别低风险人群,而整合和 SV 则表征高风险疾病。

papers.title: Exploration of immune correlates of viral clearance after PVX2 immunotherapy in patients with human papillomavirus type 16 infection and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade ≤1
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Immune responses correlated with clearance of human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) were sought in PVX2 immunotherapy-treated CIN ≤1 patients. PVX2 comprises intramuscular vaccinations with HPV16 E7-targeted pNGVL4a-Sig/E7(detox)/HSP70 DNA vaccine (3 mg, weeks 0 and 4) and HPV16 L2E7E6 fusion protein (TA-CIN; 100 μg week 8). Administering PVX2 to 12 women with HPV16+ CIN ≤1 elicited both antibody and CD8+ T-cell responses, including changes in TCR diversity, clonal expansion, and emergence of public clonotypes. HPV16 was not detected in 5/11 evaluable participants at month 6. Post-vaccination E6, E7, and L2-specific antibody titers were higher, but none correlated with clearance. Neither TCR clonal diversity/expansion nor public clonotypes were associated with HPV16 clearance. While the fractions of expanded/new clonotypes were not associated with HPV16 clearance, a higher proportion of vaccine antigen-specific reads was evident post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16. High baseline serum MCP-1 associated with HPV16 persistence, and MIP-1β trended higher post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16. IMPORTANCE HPV16 is a necessary cause of over half of all cervical cancers, and in even higher fractions of other anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. Treatments for HPV16 infection and associated pre-cancerous lesions are needed given the disease burden and limitations of current treatments. Women with persistent HPV infections endure anxiety and stress due to frequent colposcopies, inconvenience, healthcare costs from active surveillance, and potential to transmit the virus to other sexual partners. Since a majority of patients can spontaneously clear their infections, administration of an immunotherapy may promote the elimination of otherwise persistent infections where disease can progress.

papers.title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 16型感染且宫颈上皮内瘤变≤1级患者PVX2免疫治疗后病毒清除的免疫相关性探讨
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Immune responses correlated with clearance of human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) were sought in PVX2 immunotherapy-treated CIN ≤1 patients. PVX2 comprises intramuscular vaccinations with HPV16 E7-targeted pNGVL4a-Sig/E7(detox)/HSP70 DNA vaccine (3 mg, weeks 0 and 4) and HPV16 L2E7E6 fusion protein (TA-CIN; 100 μg week 8). Administering PVX2 to 12 women with HPV16+ CIN ≤1 elicited both antibody and CD8+ T-cell responses, including changes in TCR diversity, clonal expansion, and emergence of public clonotypes. HPV16 was not detected in 5/11 evaluable participants at month 6. Post-vaccination E6, E7, and L2-specific antibody titers were higher, but none correlated with clearance. Neither TCR clonal diversity/expansion nor public clonotypes were associated with HPV16 clearance. While the fractions of expanded/new clonotypes were not associated with HPV16 clearance, a higher proportion of vaccine antigen-specific reads was evident post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16. High baseline serum MCP-1 associated with HPV16 persistence, and MIP-1β trended higher post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16. IMPORTANCE HPV16 is a necessary cause of over half of all cervical cancers, and in even higher fractions of other anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. Treatments for HPV16 infection and associated pre-cancerous lesions are needed given the disease burden and limitations of current treatments. Women with persistent HPV infections endure anxiety and stress due to frequent colposcopies, inconvenience, healthcare costs from active surveillance, and potential to transmit the virus to other sexual partners. Since a majority of patients can spontaneously clear their infections, administration of an immunotherapy may promote the elimination of otherwise persistent infections where disease can progress.

papers.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

papers.title: Immunoinformatics-Driven Rational Design of Altered Peptide Ligands and In Vitro Validation of a Multi-Epitope CTL Formulation Targeting HPV16 E6/E7
papers.abstract: Background: Therapeutic vaccination against human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) is frequently limited by the weak HLA-A*02:01 presentation of native E6/E7 oncoprotein epitopes. This study aims to utilize an integrated computational-experimental pipeline to design and evaluate anchor-optimized altered peptide ligands (APLs) for improving peptide presentation and HPV16-specific T-cell responses. Methods: Anchor-residue substitutions were introduced into three wild-type E6/E7 epitopes. Candidates were prioritized in silico based on predicted presentation, affinity, immunogenicity, and toxicity, and subsequently evaluated via in vitro functional assays using HLA-A*02:01-positive donor cells and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Results: Anchor optimization successfully converted weak binders into strong binders; for instance, E6apl improved predicted affinity from 329.33 to 6.21 nM. Crucially, candidate E7apl1 exhibited normal CD8+ T-cell expansion but reduced IFN-γ secretion, revealing a distinct binding–immunogenicity dissociation. MD simulations suggested that altered peptide conformational dynamics may contribute to differences in functional activity. Subsequently, an optimized six-peptide formulation (three APLs and three wild-type epitopes) was assembled. The resulting multi-epitope HPV-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (meHPV-CTLs) mediated target-specific cytotoxicity against cervical cancer cells, achieving 74.1% ± 5.1% specific lysis at an effector-to-target ratio of 30:1, which was largely abrogated by HLA class I blockade. Conclusions: These proof-of-concept findings demonstrate that stable peptide–MHC binding is a necessary but insufficient condition for optimal T-cell activation. The experimentally characterized multi-epitope formulation provides a proof-of-concept strategy for further preclinical evaluation of HPV16-targeted peptide-based immunotherapies. Moreover, because these anchor-optimized APLs are defined at the sequence level, these sequence-defined APLs may potentially be explored in alternative vaccine delivery platforms, including mRNA-based approaches, in future studies.

Using an integrated computational-experimental pipeline, the authors introduced anchor-residue substitutions into three wild-type epitopes, prioritized candidates in silico, and validated them via in vitro functional assays and molecular dynamics simulations. papers.title_zh: 免疫信息学驱动的改变肽配体的合理设计以及针对 HPV16 E6/E7 的多表位 CTL 制剂的体外验证
papers.source_body_en: Background: Therapeutic vaccination against human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) is frequently limited by the weak HLA-A*02:01 presentation of native E6/E7 oncoprotein epitopes. This study aims to utilize an integrated computational-experimental pipeline to design and evaluate anchor-optimized altered peptide ligands (APLs) for improving peptide presentation and HPV16-specific T-cell responses. Methods: Anchor-residue substitutions were introduced into three wild-type E6/E7 epitopes. Candidates were prioritized in silico based on predicted presentation, affinity, immunogenicity, and toxicity, and subsequently evaluated via in vitro functional assays using HLA-A*02:01-positive donor cells and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Results: Anchor optimization successfully converted weak binders into strong binders; for instance, E6apl improved predicted affinity from 329.33 to 6.21 nM. Crucially, candidate E7apl1 exhibited normal CD8+ T-cell expansion but reduced IFN-γ secretion, revealing a distinct binding–immunogenicity dissociation. MD simulations suggested that altered peptide conformational dynamics may contribute to differences in functional activity. Subsequently, an optimized six-peptide formulation (three APLs and three wild-type epitopes) was assembled. The resulting multi-epitope HPV-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (meHPV-CTLs) mediated target-specific cytotoxicity against cervical cancer cells, achieving 74.1% ± 5.1% specific lysis at an effector-to-target ratio of 30:1, which was largely abrogated by HLA class I blockade. Conclusions: These proof-of-concept findings demonstrate that stable peptide–MHC binding is a necessary but insufficient condition for optimal T-cell activation. The experimentally characterized multi-epitope formulation provides a proof-of-concept strategy for further preclinical evaluation of HPV16-targeted peptide-based immunotherapies. Moreover, because these anchor-optimized APLs are defined at the sequence level, these sequence-defined APLs may potentially be explored in alternative vaccine delivery platforms, including mRNA-based approaches, in future studies.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:针对 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 (HPV16) 的治疗 疫苗接种 经常受到天然 E6/E7 癌蛋白表位较弱的 HLA-A*02:01 呈现的限制。本研究旨在利用集成的计算实验流程来设计和评估锚定优化的改变肽配体 (APL),以改善肽呈递和 HPV16 特异性 T 细胞反应。方法:将锚残基取代引入三个野生型E6/E7表位。根据预测的呈现、亲和力、免疫原性和毒性,在计算机中对候选者进行优先排序,随后使用 HLA-A*02:01 阳性供体细胞和分子动力学 (MD) 模拟通过体外功能测定进行评估。结果:Anchor优化成功将弱Binder转化为强Binder;例如,E6apl 将预测亲和力从 329.33 nM 提高到 6.21 nM。至关重要的是,候选 E7apl1 表现出正常的 CD8+ T 细胞扩增,但减少了 IFN-γ 分泌,揭示了独特的结合-免疫原性解离。MD 模拟表明,改变的肽构象动力学可能导致功能活性的差异。随后,组装了优化的六肽制剂(三个 APL 和三个野生型表位)。由此产生的多表位 HPV 特异性细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞 (meHPV-CTL) 介导针对 宫颈癌 细胞的靶标特异性细胞毒性,在效应器与靶标比率为 30:1 时实现 74.1% ± 5.1% 的特异性裂解,这在很大程度上被 HLA I 类阻断所消除。结论:这些概念验证结果表明,稳定的肽-MHC 结合是最佳 T 细胞激活的必要但不充分的条件。经过实验表征的多表位制剂为 HPV16 靶向肽免疫疗法的进一步临床前评估提供了概念验证策略。此外,由于这些锚定优化的 APL 是在序列水平上定义的,因此在未来的研究中,这些序列定义的 APL 可能会在替代的 疫苗 递送平台(包括基于 mRNA 的方法)中进行探索。

papers.title: Preclinical Development of ARV-2001, an Intradermally Administered mRNA–Lipid Nanoparticle Immunotherapeutic for the Treatment of HPV-16-Positive Cervical High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) is the principal cause of cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (cHSIL) and cervical cancer, yet the established treatments remain limited to ablative or excisional procedures that carry reproductive risk and do not eliminate the underlying infection. We report the preclinical development of ARV-2001, a messenger RNA (mRNA)–lipid nanoparticle (LNP) immunotherapeutic encoding mutated, non-oncogenic HPV-16 E6 and E7 fused to a SARS-CoV-2 spike S2 subdomain enriched in human CD4 helper epitopes, formulated in a novel cholesterol-derived ionizable lipid (ARV-T1). Methods: Interactions of ARV-2001-expressed antigens with p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) were evaluated in human cervical carcinoma cell line C33A, in lentiviral constructs in primary human keratinocytes, and in soft-agar colony-formation assays. ARV-2001 was administrated by intramuscular (IM) or intradermal (ID) injection in naive mice or in the TC-1 tumor models. Tumor size and survival were monitored over time and tumor-infiltrated lymphocytes were characterized by flow cytometry. Intracellular cytokine staining and Elispot were used to evaluate immunogenicity. Results: In vitro, the mutated E6/E7–S2 antigen lost the ability to degrade p53, to deregulate the retinoblastoma (Rb) pathway, and to support anchorage-independent growth, suggesting abrogation of oncogenic activity. The S2 domain and imiquimod administration each augmented antitumor activity and intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration while reducing myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the syngeneic HPV-16 E6/E7 TC-1 tumor models. In addition, ID administration of ARV-2001 into TC-1 tumor-bearing mice was superior to IM administration in terms of both tumor growth inhibition and survival. ID vaccination with ARV-2001 in mice consistently elicited a more potent E6/E7-specific T-cell response than the same dose given IM. Dose-escalation studies showed a dose-dependent T cell response against E6/E7 in ID-injected mice. Conclusions: This study supports future human evaluation of intradermally administrated ARV-2001 for treatment of HPV-16+ cHSIL in clinical trials.

papers.title_zh: ARV-2001 的临床前开发,一种皮内注射 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒免疫疗法,用于治疗 HPV-16 阳性宫颈高级鳞状上皮内病变的 治疗
papers.source_body_en: Background/Objective: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) is the principal cause of cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (cHSIL) and cervical cancer, yet the established treatments remain limited to ablative or excisional procedures that carry reproductive risk and do not eliminate the underlying infection. We report the preclinical development of ARV-2001, a messenger RNA (mRNA)–lipid nanoparticle (LNP) immunotherapeutic encoding mutated, non-oncogenic HPV-16 E6 and E7 fused to a SARS-CoV-2 spike S2 subdomain enriched in human CD4 helper epitopes, formulated in a novel cholesterol-derived ionizable lipid (ARV-T1). Methods: Interactions of ARV-2001-expressed antigens with p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) were evaluated in human cervical carcinoma cell line C33A, in lentiviral constructs in primary human keratinocytes, and in soft-agar colony-formation assays. ARV-2001 was administrated by intramuscular (IM) or intradermal (ID) injection in naive mice or in the TC-1 tumor models. Tumor size and survival were monitored over time and tumor-infiltrated lymphocytes were characterized by flow cytometry. Intracellular cytokine staining and Elispot were used to evaluate immunogenicity. Results: In vitro, the mutated E6/E7–S2 antigen lost the ability to degrade p53, to deregulate the retinoblastoma (Rb) pathway, and to support anchorage-independent growth, suggesting abrogation of oncogenic activity. The S2 domain and imiquimod administration each augmented antitumor activity and intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration while reducing myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the syngeneic HPV-16 E6/E7 TC-1 tumor models. In addition, ID administration of ARV-2001 into TC-1 tumor-bearing mice was superior to IM administration in terms of both tumor growth inhibition and survival. ID vaccination with ARV-2001 in mice consistently elicited a more potent E6/E7-specific T-cell response than the same dose given IM. Dose-escalation studies showed a dose-dependent T cell response against E6/E7 in ID-injected mice. Conclusions: This study supports future human evaluation of intradermally administrated ARV-2001 for treatment of HPV-16+ cHSIL in clinical trials.

papers.title: Epidemiology of Human Papillomavirus in the Middle East and North Africa: A Review of Genotypic Prevalence, Vaccination Challenges, and Non-Cervical Clinical Outcomes
papers.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the primary etiological agent of cervical cancer. Despite the high global disease burden, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region faces substantial challenges in HPV prevention and control. This narrative review aimed to synthesize existing evidence on the prevalence, genotypic distribution, awareness, vaccination status, clinical outcomes, and the role of HPV in non-cervical malignancies in the MENA region. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched, and 122 studies were included. Findings were synthesized qualitatively and descriptively. Cohort studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were prioritized to support inferences about associations and potential causal relationships. Results: HPV prevalence in the general female population of the MENA region ranged from 4.7% to 53.3%, exceeding 90% in high-risk groups and patients with malignancies. The most common genotypes were HPV16 and HPV18; however, distribution patterns varied across populations. Key risk factors included younger age, multiple sexual partners, early age at first sexual intercourse, smoking, and alcohol consumption. General awareness was low to moderate, and vaccination coverage was very low in most countries. Barriers included lack of knowledge, fear of side effects, religious concerns, and social stigma. Evidence also indicates an association between HPV and non-cervical malignancies (head and neck, esophageal, gastric, breast, and thyroid cancers), with HPV DNA detected in tumor tissues. Conclusions: HPV poses a significant public health challenge in the MENA region, characterized by high prevalence, genotypic diversity, limited knowledge and awareness, and unsatisfactory vaccination coverage. Expanding screening and vaccination through financial support, culturally and religiously appropriate education, and longitudinal studies to monitor genotypic changes and associations with other malignancies are essential measures to reduce the burden of HPV-related diseases in the region.

papers.title: Willingness to receive cross-border human papillomavirus vaccination among Chinese male university students: a cross-sectional study with statistical indirect-association analysis
papers.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an important strategy for preventing HPV-related disease among males. Access to male HPV vaccination may involve cross-border health seeking for some university students in mainland China. This study estimated willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination among Chinese male university students and examined associations of HPV-related disease recognition, awareness of cross-border vaccination availability, and demographic and informational characteristics with willingness. Methods A cross-sectional anonymous online survey was conducted between September 2025 and March 2026 among 4,260 male university students in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, and overseas. The primary outcome was willingness to travel at personal expense to Hong Kong or Macao for HPV vaccination. HPV-related disease recognition was assessed using four conditions with established HPV associations: anogenital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Of 4,260 participants, 3,182 (74.69%) reported willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination. Participants with a disease-recognition gap had substantially lower adjusted odds of willingness than those identifying at least one condition (aOR = 0.041, 95% CI: 0.017–0.095; p < 0.001). Awareness of cross-border HPV vaccination availability was positively associated with willingness (aOR = 1.233, 95% CI: 1.056–1.441; p = 0.008). Students studying in Guangdong province had higher adjusted odds of willingness than students in other mainland provinces (aOR = 1.213, 95% CI: 1.045–1.409; p = 0.011). Higher academic grade (aOR per level = 1.111, 95% CI: 1.023–1.206; p = 0.012) and exposure to school-based HPV information (aOR = 1.203, 95% CI: 1.005–1.440; p = 0.044) were also independently associated with willingness. The estimated indirect association through cross-border service awareness was statistically significant but small ( B = −0.022, bootstrap 95% CI: −0.040 to −0.006). Conclusion Willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination was reported by approximately three-quarters of participants. Recognition of established HPV-related male diseases and awareness of cross-border vaccination availability were associated with willingness. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether male-focused HPV education and service-navigation strategies increase actual vaccine uptake.

papers.title: Analysis of the clinical utility of p16/Ki-67 dual staining in screening cervical lesions among women positive for high-risk HPV
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is closely associated with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV). Although HPV testing offers high sensitivity, its limited specificity may result in excessive colposcopy referrals, and the triage performance of traditional liquid-based cytology (TCT) remains suboptimal among hrHPV-positive women. As a biomarker reflecting HPV-mediated cell-cycle dysregulation and aberrant proliferation, p16/Ki-67 dual staining has shown potential advantages in identifying clinically significant high-grade cervical lesions. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical utility of p16/Ki-67 dual staining in screening cervical lesions among hrHPV-positive women and to explore its role in optimizing referral strategies. Retrospectively, this single-center cohort study included 100 consecutive hrHPV-positive women who attended our clinic between October 2024 and October 2025. All participants underwent hrHPV genotyping, TCT, and p16/Ki-67 dual staining during the same visit, followed by colposcopy and histopathological assessment. Histology served as the reference standard. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of p16/Ki-67 for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2+ (CIN2+) lesions and compared it with TCT, HPV genotyping, and a combined triage model (hrHPV + TCT + p16/Ki-67). In addition, we simulated the screening efficiency of different colposcopy referral strategies. Among the 100 hrHPV-positive women included, 35 (35.0%) were diagnosed with CIN2+. papers.title: Fractional-Order Mathematical Modeling of Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) Using Artificial Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The study proposes a mathematical framework to evaluate the HPV infection transmission dynamics, taking into account advanced approaches related to fractional calculus. The HPV infection and cervical cancer is always a major public health threat across the world, particularly in those areas having insufficient availability to health care services and control interventions. In first step, the positivity and boundedness of solutions are precisely examined to show that the model remains biologically valuable in the long run. In this study the disease free equilibrium and endemic equilibrium is provided to describe the long term behavior of the disease in a population. The basic reproductive number and sensitivity analysis is also studied as it is vital to analyse behavior of the dynamics. The theoretical results is establish for the model under consideration using fixed point theory. Next, the condition for Hyers-Ulam’s (H-U) type stability is clearly demonstrated. Then, applying the modified Euler’s method (MEM) for the computation of numerical solution of the proposed model. At the end, we give graphical representation of the involved results. We use some real values for the parameters involved in our considered model. Matlab is used for graphical demonstration. Through a comprehensive numerical analysis, the model explores how various fractional order values inuence the dynamics of HPV transmission. Hence, revealing suggestions for how fractional order may better convey the intricate relationships within the communities. These development also draw awareness to the method’s significance in advancing disease modeling and deepening our knowledge of HPV transmission. With the help of artificial deep neural networks (DNNs), we investigate the considered model. We deduced some statistical thresholds including mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) together with progressional analysis. Further, graphical illustrations are given for infected classes using different fractional order. Absolute error between the simulated and those predicted by DNNs are compared for various fractional orders.

In first step, the positivity and boundedness of solutions are precisely examined to show that the model remains biologically valuable in the long run. In this study the disease free equilibrium and endemic equilibrium is provided to describe the long term behavior of the disease in a population. The basic reproductive number and sensitivity analysis is also studied as it is vital to analyse behavior of the dynamics. The theoretical results is establish for the model under consideration using fixed point theory. Next, the condition for Hyers-Ulam’s (H-U) type stability is clearly demonstrated. Then, applying the modified Euler’s method (MEM) for the computation of numerical solution of the proposed model. At the end, we give graphical representation of the involved results. We use some real values for the parameters involved in our considered model. Matlab is used for graphical demonstration. Through a comprehensive numerical analysis, the model explores how various fractional order values inuence the dynamics of HPV transmission. Hence, revealing suggestions for how fractional order may better convey the intricate relationships within the communities. These development also draw awareness to the method’s significance in advancing disease modeling and deepening our knowledge of HPV transmission. With the help of artificial deep neural networks (DNNs), we investigate the considered model. We deduced some statistical thresholds including mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) together with progressional analysis. Further, graphical illustrations are given for infected classes using different fractional order. Absolute error between the simulated and those predicted by DNNs are compared for various fractional orders.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study develops a theoretical mathematical model of HPV infection transmission dynamics, examining disease-free and endemic equilibria to describe long-term behavior without specifying a human population or clinical setting.
analysis.methods: The authors use fixed point theory to establish theoretical results, apply the modified Euler’s method for numerical solutions, and employ artificial deep neural networks (DNNs) to investigate the model, including computation of mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) for validation.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as revealing how fractional order values influence HPV transmission dynamics, suggesting that fractional calculus may better capture complex community relationships, and highlight the method’s significance in advancing disease modeling.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings imply that fractional-order mathematical modeling combined with artificial neural networks could improve understanding of HPV transmission patterns, potentially informing surveillance and control strategies in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is theoretical and abstract-only, lacking empirical validation in human populations or clinical data, which limits its direct applicability to public health practice and warrants a low confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study proposes a fractional-order mathematical model to analyze HPV transmission dynamics using artificial deep neural networks (DNNs). The authors establish theoretical stability conditions and use numerical methods to simulate disease behavior, including disease-free and endemic equilibria. They demonstrate Hyers-Ulam stability and compare simulated results with DNN predictions across fractional orders, providing graphical illustrations of infected classes. The work suggests fractional calculus may better represent complex transmission patterns in communities. However, the analysis is entirely theoretical with no empirical validation, limiting its immediate public health relevance and indicating low confidence in applicability.

papers.abstract_zh: 该研究提出了一个数学框架来评估 HPV 感染 传播 动态,同时考虑到与分数阶微积分相关的先进方法。HPV 感染和 宫颈癌 始终是世界各地的主要公共卫生威胁,特别是在那些医疗保健服务和控制干预措施不足的地区。第一步,精确检查解的正性和有界性,以表明该模型从长远来看仍然具有生物学价值。在本研究中,提供无病平衡和地方病平衡来描述疾病在人群中的长期行为。还研究了基本繁殖数和敏感性分析,因为它对于分析动力学行为至关重要。理论结果是使用不动点理论为所考虑的模型建立的。接下来,清楚地证明了 Hyers-Ulam (H-U) 型稳定性的条件。然后,应用修正欧拉方法(MEM)计算所提出模型的数值解。最后,我们给出了所涉及结果的图形表示。我们对我们考虑的模型中涉及的参数使用一些实际值。使用Matlab进行图形演示。通过全面的数值分析,该模型探讨了各种分数阶值如何影响 HPV 传播 的动态。因此,揭示了分数阶如何更好地传达社区内复杂关系的建议。这些进展也让人们认识到该方法在推进疾病建模和加深我们对 HPV 传播 的了解方面的重要性。在人工深度神经网络 (DNN) 的帮助下,我们研究了所考虑的模型。我们通过渐进分析推导出一些统计阈值,包括均方误差(MSE)和均方根误差(RMSE)。此外,还使用不同的分数阶对受感染类别进行了图示。对不同分数阶的模拟结果和 DNN 预测结果之间的绝对误差进行了比较。

papers.title: The cervicovaginal microbiome: an emerging determinant of HPV infection and disease
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are epitheliotropic viruses that cause diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers. HPVs exhibit tropism for the epithelial lining of the skin, oral cavity, and anogenital tract. A subset of HPVs, known as high-risk HPVs, have oncogenic potential and cause nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including essentially all cervical cancers, most other anogenital cancers, and a growing percentage of head and neck cancers. A large and growing body of clinical and epidemiological research has established the host microbiome, or the collection of microorganisms on and within the body, as a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. In this review, an overview of the current understanding of associations between bacterial components of the host cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) and aspects of HPV pathogenesis is discussed. Potential mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV infection and neoplastic disease development are also presented. The inherent challenges of studying HPVs and the microbiome have impeded progress to define not only the underlying mechanisms involved in HPV-CVM interactions, but also the ability to address remaining questions such as causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. Emerging in vitro and in vivo models provide powerful opportunities to address these outstanding questions and increase our understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and subsequent disease.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPVs), their epitheliotropic nature, and their role in causing diseases such as cutaneous warts, anogenital cancers, and head and neck cancers, focusing on the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) as a determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes clinical and epidemiological research on the host microbiome, specifically the bacterial components of the CVM, and discusses potential mechanisms by which the CVM influences HPV pathogenesis. It highlights the challenges in studying HPV-microbiome interactions and the need for advanced models to address causality, temporal dynamics, and directionality.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: High-risk HPVs, including HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV45, HPV52, and HPV58, are established as oncogenic agents responsible for nearly one-third of virus-associated cancers globally, including essentially all cervical cancers and a significant proportion of anogenital and head and neck cancers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The inherent challenges in studying HPVs and the microbiome impede progress in defining the underlying mechanisms of HPV-CVM interactions, as well as addressing causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. The review notes that these gaps persist despite emerging in vitro and in vivo models.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Emerging in vitro and in vivo models are identified as critical tools to address outstanding questions about HPV-CVM interactions, including causality and temporal dynamics, thereby advancing understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and disease.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPVs), their epitheliotropic properties, and their association with diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to cancers. It highlights high-risk HPVs, such as HPV16 and HPV18, as oncogenic drivers of a substantial global cancer burden. The cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) is emphasized as a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease progression, with potential mechanisms of interaction discussed. However, challenges in studying HPV-microbiome dynamics, including causality and temporal relationships, remain unresolved. The review underscores the need for advanced experimental models to elucidate these interactions and guide future research and clinical strategies.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPVs), their epitheliotropic nature, and their role in causing diseases such as cutaneous warts, anogenital cancers, and head and neck cancers, focusing on the cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) as a determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes clinical and epidemiological research on the host microbiome, specifically the bacterial components of the CVM, and discusses potential mechanisms by which the CVM influences HPV pathogenesis. It highlights the challenges in studying HPV-microbiome interactions and the need for advanced models to address causality, temporal dynamics, and directionality.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: High-risk HPVs, including HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV45, HPV52, and HPV58, are established as oncogenic agents responsible for nearly one-third of virus-associated cancers globally, including essentially all cervical cancers and a significant proportion of anogenital and head and neck cancers.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The inherent challenges in studying HPVs and the microbiome impede progress in defining the underlying mechanisms of HPV-CVM interactions, as well as addressing causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. The review notes that these gaps persist despite emerging in vitro and in vivo models.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Emerging in vitro and in vivo models are identified as critical tools to address outstanding questions about HPV-CVM interactions, including causality and temporal dynamics, thereby advancing understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and disease.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)、其亲上皮性质及其在引起皮肤疣、肛门生殖器癌和头颈癌等疾病中的作用,重点关注宫颈阴道微生物组 (CVM) 作为 HPV 感染、持续性和疾病发展的决定因素。

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 高危型HPV,包括 HPV16、HPV18、HPV31、HPV33、HPV45、HPV52 和 HPV58,被确定为致癌因子,导致全球近三分之一的病毒相关癌症,包括基本上所有 宫颈癌 以及相当比例的肛门生殖器癌和头颈癌。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究 HPV 和微生物组的固有挑战阻碍了在定义 HPV-CVM 相互作用的潜在机制以及解决这种关系的因果关系、时间动态和方向性方面取得进展。该评论指出,尽管出现了体外和体内模型,但这些差距仍然存在。

papers.title_zh: 宫颈阴道微生物组:HPV 感染和疾病的新决定因素
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are epitheliotropic viruses that cause diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers. HPVs exhibit tropism for the epithelial lining of the skin, oral cavity, and anogenital tract. A subset of HPVs, known as high-risk HPVs, have oncogenic potential and cause nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including essentially all cervical cancers, most other anogenital cancers, and a growing percentage of head and neck cancers. A large and growing body of clinical and epidemiological research has established the host microbiome, or the collection of microorganisms on and within the body, as a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. In this review, an overview of the current understanding of associations between bacterial components of the host cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) and aspects of HPV pathogenesis is discussed. Potential mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV infection and neoplastic disease development are also presented. The inherent challenges of studying HPVs and the microbiome have impeded progress to define not only the underlying mechanisms involved in HPV-CVM interactions, but also the ability to address remaining questions such as causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. Emerging in vitro and in vivo models provide powerful opportunities to address these outstanding questions and increase our understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and subsequent disease.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 是一种亲上皮病毒,可引起从皮肤疣到侵袭性癌症等多种疾病。HPV 对皮肤、口腔和肛门生殖道的上皮衬里表现出趋向性。HPV 的一个子集(称为 高危型HPV)具有致癌潜力,导致全球近三分之一的病毒相关癌症,包括基本上所有 宫颈癌、大多数其他肛门生殖器癌症以及越来越多的头颈癌。大量且不断增长的临床和流行病学研究已将 宿主 微生物组(即体内和体外的微生物集合)确定为 HPV 感染、持续存在和疾病发展的关键决定因素。在这篇综述中,概述了目前对 宿主 宫颈阴道微生物组 (CVM) 细菌成分与 HPV 发病机制 各方面之间关联的理解。还介绍了 CVM 影响 HPV 感染和肿瘤疾病发展的潜在机制。研究 HPV 和微生物组的固有挑战不仅阻碍了定义 HPV-CVM 相互作用的潜在机制的进展,而且也阻碍了解决诸如因果关系、时间动态和这种关系的方向性等剩余问题的能力。新兴的体外和体内模型为解决这些突出问题提供了强大的机会,并增加我们对导致 HPV 感染和随后疾病的跨界相互作用的理解。

papers.title: The Prevalence of Human Papilloma Virus in Turkish Women
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The prevalence of Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) in Türkiye may vary from that reported in other countries. Determining the age-specific distribution of HPV infection and its overall prevalence in all tested individuals, supported by a large sample size, would provide valuable insights for HPV prevention programs. This study aims to determine the regional prevalence of HPV infection. Methods: This is a retrospective study containing data from 52,930 patients who underwent HPV testing at a tertiary hospital between 2016 and 2024. Patients aged 21 to 65 were included in the study. Target DNA amplification by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and nucleic acid hybridization techniques were performed for the identification of HPV. Overall prevalence, age-specific prevalence, and genotype distribution were examined. Results: Analysis of genotype distribution revealed that isolated HPV16 positivity was 4.0% (n = 2118), isolated HPV18 positivity was 1.0% (n = 528), and isolated other high-risk (HR) HPV types (excluding HPV16 and HPV18) were detected in 10.8% (n = 5693) of patients. The co-positivity rates were as follows: HPV16 and HPV18 in 0.4% (n = 237), HPV16 and HR-HPV other in 2.3% (n = 1197), HPV18 and HR-HPV other in 1.0% (n = 513), and HPV16, HPV18, and HR-HPV other in 0.3% (n = 145). Conclusions: This study highlights that HPV positivity is higher among individuals aged 21–24 years in our population, the overall prevalence is broadly consistent with the range reported in previous Turkish and international studies, and the pooled other HR-HPV group was more frequent than HPV16 or HPV18 individually.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to characterize the prevalence of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) in Türkiye, noting that reported prevalence may differ from other countries and that age-specific distribution data are valuable for prevention programs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study analyzed data from 52,930 patients aged 21 to 65 who underwent HPV testing at a tertiary hospital between 2016 and 2024.
analysis.methods: HPV identification was performed using target DNA amplification by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and nucleic acid hybridization techniques. Overall prevalence, age-specific prevalence, and genotype distribution were examined.
analysis.main_results: Isolated HPV16 positivity was 4.0% (n = 2118), isolated HPV18 positivity was 1.0% (n = 528), and isolated other high-risk (HR) HPV types (excluding HPV16 and HPV18) were detected in 10.8% (n = 5693) of patients. Co-positivity rates included HPV16 and HPV18 in 0.4% (n = 237), HPV16 and HR-HPV other in 2.3% (n = 1197), HPV18 and HR-HPV other in 1.0% (n = 513), and HPV16, HPV18, and HR-HPV other in 0.3% (n = 145).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets that HPV positivity is higher among individuals aged 21–24 years, the overall prevalence aligns with prior Turkish and international reports, and the pooled other HR-HPV group was more frequent than HPV16 or HPV18 individually.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform HPV prevention programs by providing regional prevalence data and age-specific distribution patterns to guide vaccination and screening strategies in Türkiye.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, single-centre setting, and reliance on PCR-based testing without clinical outcome data, which constrains generalisability and causal inference; evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed HPV test results from 52,930 patients aged 21–65 at a Turkish tertiary hospital (2016–2024) to determine regional prevalence and genotype distribution. Using PCR and nucleic acid hybridization, it found isolated HPV16 in 4.0%, HPV18 in 1.0%, and other high-risk HPV types in 10.8% of patients, with co-infections in up to 2.3%. HPV positivity was highest in the 21–24 age group, and the pooled other HR-HPV group exceeded HPV16 or HPV18 individually. The authors conclude that these patterns are consistent with prior Turkish and international reports. The findings support targeted HPV prevention programs but are limited by retrospective design, single-centre data, and lack of clinical outcomes, warranting cautious interpretation.

papers.title_zh: 土耳其女性中人乳头瘤病毒的 患病率
papers.source_body_en: Background/Objectives: The prevalence of Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) in Türkiye may vary from that reported in other countries. Determining the age-specific distribution of HPV infection and its overall prevalence in all tested individuals, supported by a large sample size, would provide valuable insights for HPV prevention programs. This study aims to determine the regional prevalence of HPV infection. Methods: This is a retrospective study containing data from 52,930 patients who underwent HPV testing at a tertiary hospital between 2016 and 2024. Patients aged 21 to 65 were included in the study. Target DNA amplification by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and nucleic acid hybridization techniques were performed for the identification of HPV. Overall prevalence, age-specific prevalence, and genotype distribution were examined. Results: Analysis of genotype distribution revealed that isolated HPV16 positivity was 4.0% (n = 2118), isolated HPV18 positivity was 1.0% (n = 528), and isolated other high-risk (HR) HPV types (excluding HPV16 and HPV18) were detected in 10.8% (n = 5693) of patients. The co-positivity rates were as follows: HPV16 and HPV18 in 0.4% (n = 237), HPV16 and HR-HPV other in 2.3% (n = 1197), HPV18 and HR-HPV other in 1.0% (n = 513), and HPV16, HPV18, and HR-HPV other in 0.3% (n = 145). Conclusions: This study highlights that HPV positivity is higher among individuals aged 21–24 years in our population, the overall prevalence is broadly consistent with the range reported in previous Turkish and international studies, and the pooled other HR-HPV group was more frequent than HPV16 or HPV18 individually.

papers.title: The human papillomavirus L2 protein in the capsid is an ensemble of related structures poised to exit the virus particle
papers.abstract: The human papillomavirus (HPV) capsid contains 360 molecules of the L1 protein, which assembles into pentamers that form the capsid shell, and up to 72 molecules of the L2 protein. The C-terminus of the L2 protein must emerge from the capsid, insert into the endosome membrane, and protrude into the cytoplasm to bind to cellular proteins that mediate trafficking of the virus to the nucleus during virus entry. Computational analysis predicts that much of L2 is disordered, but the stoichiometry, structure and location of L2 in the capsid remain elusive. Here, we use cryo-EM single particle analysis of HPV16 pseudovirus capsids with and without the L2 protein combined with AlphaFold3 predictions and molecular dynamics simulations to develop a structural model of L2 within the capsid. Our results revealed that a single molecule of L2 associates with the inner surface of most L1 pentamers. The relatively rigid structure of the pentamer forces the long intrinsically disordered segments of L2 to adopt numerous related, compact, stable conformations in the capsid, whereas the structured elements of L2 remain folded but adopt varied positions in space largely beneath the pentamer. A finger-like projection of L2 extends into the central pore of the pentamer, but many different segments of the disordered domains of L2 can form fingers. In some models the C-terminus of L2 extends through the pore to the exterior surface of the capsid positioned to insert into the endosomal membrane. Consistent with these models, analysis of purified pseudoviruses showed that the C-terminus of multiple L2 molecules is exposed on the surface of each capsid. These findings provide a structural basis for understanding how L2 is organized in the capsid poised to initiate its action during virus entry.

papers.title_zh: 衣壳中的 人乳头瘤病毒 L2 蛋白是准备离开病毒颗粒的相关结构的集合
papers.source_body_en: The human papillomavirus (HPV) capsid contains 360 molecules of the L1 protein, which assembles into pentamers that form the capsid shell, and up to 72 molecules of the L2 protein. The C-terminus of the L2 protein must emerge from the capsid, insert into the endosome membrane, and protrude into the cytoplasm to bind to cellular proteins that mediate trafficking of the virus to the nucleus during virus entry. Computational analysis predicts that much of L2 is disordered, but the stoichiometry, structure and location of L2 in the capsid remain elusive. Here, we use cryo-EM single particle analysis of HPV16 pseudovirus capsids with and without the L2 protein combined with AlphaFold3 predictions and molecular dynamics simulations to develop a structural model of L2 within the capsid. Our results revealed that a single molecule of L2 associates with the inner surface of most L1 pentamers. The relatively rigid structure of the pentamer forces the long intrinsically disordered segments of L2 to adopt numerous related, compact, stable conformations in the capsid, whereas the structured elements of L2 remain folded but adopt varied positions in space largely beneath the pentamer. A finger-like projection of L2 extends into the central pore of the pentamer, but many different segments of the disordered domains of L2 can form fingers. In some models the C-terminus of L2 extends through the pore to the exterior surface of the capsid positioned to insert into the endosomal membrane. Consistent with these models, analysis of purified pseudoviruses showed that the C-terminus of multiple L2 molecules is exposed on the surface of each capsid. These findings provide a structural basis for understanding how L2 is organized in the capsid poised to initiate its action during virus entry.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 衣壳包含 360 个 L1 蛋白分子(可组装成形成衣壳壳的五聚体)和最多 72 个 L2 蛋白分子。L2 蛋白的 C 末端必须从衣壳中出现,插入内体膜,并突出到细胞质中,以与在病毒进入过程中介导病毒运输到细胞核的细胞蛋白结合。计算分析预测 L2 的大部分是无序的,但衣壳中 L2 的化学计量、结构和位置仍然难以捉摸。在这里,我们使用冷冻电镜单粒子分析含有和不含有 L2 蛋白的 HPV16 假病毒衣壳,并结合 AlphaFold3 预测和分子动力学模拟,开发衣壳内 L2 的结构模型。我们的结果表明,L2 的单个分子与大多数 L1 五聚体的内表面结合。五聚体相对刚性的结构迫使L2的长的本质上无序的片段在衣壳中采用许多相关的、紧凑的、稳定的构象,而L2的结构元件保持折叠,但在主要位于五聚体下方的空间中采用不同的位置。L2 的手指状突起延伸到五聚体的中心孔中,但 L2 无序结构域的许多不同片段可以形成手指。在一些模型中,L2 的 C 末端穿过孔延伸至衣壳的外表面,定位为插入内体膜。与这些模型一致,对纯化的假病毒的分析表明,多个 L2 分子的 C 末端暴露在每个衣壳的表面。这些发现为理解 L2 在衣壳中如何组织以在病毒进入期间启动其作用提供了结构基础。

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Limited research has explored the relationships among genetic polymorphisms, viral load, adaptability, persistence, and pathogenicity of human papillomavirus (HPV) type 16. Understanding these associations is essential for clarifying HPV16 pathogenic mechanisms and improving prevention, screening, and control strategies. Methods: Female subjects attending three hospitals in Baghdad, Iraq—Al-Alawiyah Hospital, Al-Habibyah Hospital, and Baghdad Teaching Hospital—were enrolled. Exfoliated cervical cell samples were collected. HPV genotyping and viral load quantification were performed using real-time fluorescence polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and the E6 and E7 oncogenes were sequenced using Sanger sequencing. Analyses focused on temporal trends in HPV16 detection, distribution of HPV16 lineages and sublineages (A–D), and E6/E7 sequence variants. Associations between viral lineage, viral load, pathogenicity, and persistence were also evaluated. Results: Of 3,453 samples analyzed, HPV infection was detected in 974 individuals. HPV16 was identified in 162 HPV-positive cases, yielding an overall prevalence of 6.16%. Significant differences in HPV16 detection rates were observed between 2022 and 2025. The HPV16 lineage A prototype, with E6 and E7 sequences identical to the reference genome, was the most prevalent lineage. This dominant lineage was associated with an increased risk of persistent infection and cervical disease, including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer. Viral load differed significantly between disease and lesion-free groups, as well as between persistent infection and viral clearance groups. No significant association was observed between viral load and E6/E7 mutations (E6 L83V or E7 N29S). Conclusions: The HPV16 lineage A prototype plays a key role in viral pathogenicity and persistence. Viral load correlates positively with disease severity and persistence, suggesting its potential utility as a clinical biomarker. Further studies are needed to clarify additional molecular mechanisms underlying HPV16 evolution and adaptation. Acknowledgements We sincerely thank all the researchers of our research team involved in this study. Funding No funding was provided for this manuscript. All the participants signed an informed consent form before the collection of samples. All participants and data were blinded to maintain the confidentiality of the participants. analysis.methods: HPV genotyping and viral load quantification were performed using real-time fluorescence polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and the E6 and E7 oncogenes were sequenced using Sanger sequencing to evaluate temporal trends in HPV16 detection, lineage distribution, and associations between viral lineage, viral load, pathogenicity, and persistence.
analysis.main_results: Of 3,453 samples analyzed, HPV16 was identified in 162 HPV-positive cases, yielding an overall prevalence of 6.16%, with significant differences in HPV16 detection rates between 2022 and 2025. The HPV16 lineage A prototype was the most prevalent and was associated with increased risk of persistent infection and cervical disease, including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genetic polymorphism, pathogenicity, and persistent infection capacity of HPV16 by analyzing 3,453 cervical samples from female subjects in Baghdad, Iraq. Using real-time PCR and Sanger sequencing, researchers identified HPV16 in 162 cases (6.16% prevalence) and found that lineage A was dominant and associated with increased risk of persistent infection and cervical disease. Viral load differed significantly between disease states and infection outcomes, though no association with E6/E7 mutations was detected. The authors conclude that lineage A plays a key role in pathogenicity and persistence, and propose viral load as a potential biomarker for disease severity and persistence. The study is constrained by its regional scope and the need for further mechanistic research, indicating moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 有限的研究探索了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 16 型的基因多态性、病毒载量、适应性、持久性和致病性之间的关系,造成了关于其致病机制和临床意义的知识空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 招募了在伊拉克巴格达三家医院(Al-Alawiyah 医院、Al-Habibyah 医院和巴格达教学医院)就诊的女性受试者,并收集脱落的宫颈细胞样本进行分析。
elements_zh.methods: 使用实时荧光聚合酶链式反应 (PCR) 进行 HPV 基因分型和病毒载量定量,并使用桑格测序对 E6 和 E7 癌基因进行测序,以评估 HPV16 检测、谱系分布以及病毒谱系、病毒载量、致病性和持久性之间的关联的时间趋势。
elements_zh.main_results: 在分析的 3,453 个样本中,在 162 例 HPV 阳性病例中鉴定出 HPV16,总体 患病率 为 6.16%,2022 年至 2025 年 HPV16 检出率存在显着差异。HPV16 谱系 A 原型最为普遍,与持续感染和宫颈疾病(包括宫颈上皮内瘤变和 宫颈癌)风险增加相关。疾病组和无病变组之间以及持续感染组和病毒清除组之间的病毒载量存在显着差异,但病毒载量与 E6/E7 突变(E6 L83V 或 E7 N29S)之间没有观察到显着关联。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HPV16 谱系 A 原型在病毒致病性和持久性中发挥着关键作用,并且病毒载量与疾病严重程度和持久性呈正相关,这表明其作为临床生物标志物的潜在用途。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能通过强调 A 谱系在持续感染和疾病进展中的重要性,为 HPV16 监测 策略提供信息,并且可以支持使用病毒载量作为临床环境中风险分层的生物标志物。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其重点关注单一地理区域,并且需要进一步研究以阐明 HPV16 进化 和适应的其他分子机制,需要中等强度的证据。

The HPV16 lineage A prototype was the most prevalent and was associated with increased risk of persistent infection and cervical disease, including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer. Viral load differed significantly between disease and lesion-free groups, as well as between persistent infection and viral clearance groups, but no significant association was observed between viral load and E6/E7 mutations (E6 L83V or E7 N29S).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the HPV16 lineage A prototype plays a key role in viral pathogenicity and persistence, and that viral load correlates positively with disease severity and persistence, suggesting its potential utility as a clinical biomarker.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform HPV16 surveillance strategies by highlighting the importance of lineage A in persistent infection and disease progression, and could support the use of viral load as a biomarker for risk stratification in clinical settings.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single geographic region and the need for further research to clarify additional molecular mechanisms underlying HPV16 evolution and adaptation, warranting a moderate strength of evidence.
